exposure: adherence to guidelines for diagnosing failed induction of labor (FIOL) and arrest of dilation (AOD)
duration of oxytocin use after rupture of membranes
outcome: Rate of adherence to ACOG guidelines
cohort: Singleton pregnancies resulting in primary cesarean deliveries for failed induction of labor or arrest of dilation
finding: Non-compliance with ACOG guidelines for diagnosing failed induction of labor and arrest of dilation was high, but adherence to these guidelines was associated with lower physician cesarean delivery rates without increasing obstetric or neonatal complications.
mod_finding: Adherence to the American College of Obstetrics and Gynecology guidelines for diagnosing failed induction of labor and arrest of dilation was associated with lower physician C-section rates.
birth_weight: Birth weight was statistically higher in adherent cesarean deliveries.
